scores.evidence: MVP: catalog with versioning, flat/seat subscriptions, PSP integration with webhook inbox, invoices, basic dunning, ledger, entitlements.
scores.rationale: Phases roughly go core then usage then enterprise then scale, but the MVP bundles everything and the ledger is listed after invoices and payments, so the ordering isn't clearly substrate-first.

scores.evidence: MVP: catalog with versioning, flat/seat subscriptions, PSP integration with webhook inbox, invoices, basic dunning, ledger, entitlements.
scores.rationale: The MVP is a feature bundle, not a thin end-to-end slice running in production first.

scores.evidence: Fail-open vs. fail-closed is decided per feature. Usually fail-open for core access and fail-closed for expensive overages.
scores.rationale: Some decisions have defaults (pooled vs silo, build vs buy, proration policy), but there is no consolidated irreversible-decision list and no explicit flip conditions.

scores.evidence: Abstract this behind a tenant→cell routing table from day one.
scores.rationale: Some widest-impact items are placed early (tenant routing, RLS, immutable invariants), but no explicit blast-radius ordering appears within phases.

scores.evidence: PCI: collect cards with the PSP's hosted fields or elements and store only tokens.
scores.rationale: Security is covered in detail in standalone sections (RLS, PCI, RBAC) but isn't tied to the phases.

scores.evidence: SLOs: ingestion durability (no lost events), invoice finalization within N minutes of period end, and entitlement p99 latency.
scores.rationale: There are only SLOs and alerts in a standalone section, with no observability in Phase 0 or any later phase.

scores.evidence: Test clocks: let a subscription run against simulated time.
scores.rationale: Test clocks, raw events kept for re-rating and shadow re-rate rehearsal support reproducibility, but there is nothing on environments or builds and nothing threaded per phase.

scores.evidence: Exactly-once effects come from idempotency keys plus unique constraints plus the inbox/outbox pattern.
scores.rationale: Resilience is strong in the design (inbox/outbox, kill switches, reconciliation) but sits in standalone sections, not per phase.
The plan never addresses whether an AI layer applies, so there is no N/A declaration.

scores.evidence: Scale and finance: cells, reconciliation automation, RevRec feed, e-invoicing, re-rating tooling.
scores.rationale: Later work is deferred into phases 2–4, but there are no explicit pull-forward conditions.

note: The plan is a strong domain architecture, but it has weak phase discipline: no walking skeleton, no observability per phase, and no AI N/A declaration.
